name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q01 - Straight chain structure confirmation of glucose molecule

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Glucose on prolonged heating with hydroiodic acid (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) forms \(n\)-hexane.

Statement II: The formation of \(n\)-hexane confirms that all six carbon atoms in glucose are linked in a continuous straight chain.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The chemical structure of monosaccharides was historically elucidated through functional group reactions and reductive degradation. Prolonged reaction with strong reducing agents like hydroiodic acid at high temperatures removes all oxygen atoms, yielding the corresponding alkane backbone.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
When D-glucose (\(\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}\)) is heated with concentrated hydroiodic acid (\(\mathrm{HI}\)) and red phosphorus over prolonged time, it undergoes complete reduction of its carbonyl and hydroxyl groups to form the six-carbon straight-chain alkane, \(n\)-hexane (\(\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_4CH_3}\)). Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Because \(n\)-hexane has an unbranched, straight chain of six carbon atoms, its isolation from the reduction of glucose proves that no skeletal rearrangement occurred and that the carbon skeleton of glucose consists of all six carbons linked sequentially in an unbranched chain. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q02 - Classification and solubility characteristics of vitamins

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Vitamin B group and vitamin C are fat-soluble vitamins and can be stored in adipose tissues.

Statement II: Vitamin A and vitamin D are water-soluble vitamins that must be supplied regularly in the diet because they are readily excreted in urine.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Vitamins are classified into two major groups based on their solubility: water-soluble vitamins and fat-soluble vitamins. Fat-soluble vitamins dissolve in lipids and are stored in the liver and adipose tissues, whereas water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine (with the exception of vitamin \(\mathrm{B}_{12}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Vitamin B complex and vitamin C are water-soluble vitamins, not fat-soluble. Because of their high solubility in water, they are readily filtered by the kidneys and excreted in urine, meaning they cannot be stored in large quantities in adipose tissues (except \(\mathrm{B}_{12}\)). Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble vitamins, not water-soluble. They dissolve in fats and oils, are stored in adipose tissue and the liver, and are not readily excreted in urine. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q03 - Glycosidic linkages in maltose and lactose

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Maltose is a reducing disaccharide composed of two \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units joined by a C1–C4 glycosidic linkage.

Statement II: Lactose is a non-reducing sugar because the hemiacetal groups of both galactose and glucose are involved in forming the glycosidic linkage.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Disaccharides consist of two monosaccharide units connected by an oxide linkage called a glycosidic linkage. A disaccharide is classified as reducing if it possesses a free hemiacetal or hemiketal group at an anomeric carbon capable of opening to yield a free aldehyde or ketone group.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Maltose is formed from two \(\alpha\)-D-glucose molecules linked between C-1 of the first unit and C-4 of the second unit (\(\alpha\)-1,4-glycosidic bond). The C-1 position of the second glucose unit remains free as a hemiacetal that can reduce Fehling's and Tollens' reagents. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Lactose (milk sugar) is composed of \(\beta\)-D-galactose and \(\beta\)-D-glucose linked via a \(\beta\)-1,4-glycosidic bond (C-1 of galactose to C-4 of glucose). Although C-1 of galactose is bonded, C-1 of the glucose unit is a free hemiacetal group that can open into a free aldehyde in solution. Consequently, lactose is a reducing sugar, not a non-reducing sugar. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q04 - Structural comparison of amylose and amylopectin

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Amylose is a highly branched-chain polymer of glucose constituting about 80–85% of starch and is insoluble in water.

Statement II: Amylopectin is a branched-chain polymer of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units in which the linear chain is formed by C1–C4 glycosidic linkages and branching occurs via C1–C6 glycosidic linkages.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Starch is composed of two macromolecular polysaccharide fractions: amylose and amylopectin, which differ markedly in their chain linearity, branching, solubility, and relative proportions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Amylose is a water-soluble component that constitutes only about 15–20% of starch. Chemically, amylose is a long unbranched linear chain of 200–1000 \(\alpha\)-D-(+)-glucose units held exclusively by C1–C4 glycosidic linkages. It is amylopectin, not amylose, that is insoluble in water and constitutes 80–85% of starch. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Amylopectin is an insoluble, highly branched polymer. The main linear backbone consists of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose units linked by C1–C4 glycosidic bonds, while branch points occur periodically through C1–C6 glycosidic linkages with side chains. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q05 - Pentose sugar and base compositions in polynucleotides

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Complete chemical hydrolysis of DNA yields the pentose sugar \(\beta\)-D-ribose along with the pyrimidine base uracil.

Statement II: In RNA molecules, the sugar moiety is \(\beta\)-D-2-deoxyribose and thymine replaces cytosine as one of the major pyrimidine bases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are biopolymers composed of repeating nucleotide monomers. Each monomer consists of a nitrogenous heterocyclic base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group. DNA and RNA differ fundamentally in both their sugar moiety and pyrimidine base identity.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) contains \(\beta\)-D-2-deoxyribose as its sugar moiety, not \(\beta\)-D-ribose. Furthermore, the four nitrogenous bases in DNA are adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T); uracil (U) is completely absent from DNA. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
RNA (ribonucleic acid) contains \(\beta\)-D-ribose, not 2-deoxyribose. Moreover, the pyrimidine bases in RNA are cytosine (C) and uracil (U); thymine is absent in standard RNA, and uracil replaces thymine (not cytosine). Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q06 - Endocrine regulation of carbohydrate metabolism and stress

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Insulin and glucagon act antagonistically to maintain blood glucose concentrations within a narrow physiological range.

Statement II: Glucocorticoids secreted by the adrenal cortex regulate carbohydrate metabolism, modulate inflammatory reactions, and are involved in responses to stress.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Hormones act as intercellular chemical messengers produced by endocrine glands. They coordinate metabolic homeostasis, blood sugar regulation, and physiological responses to stress.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
Insulin is a polypeptide hormone released by the pancreas in response to rising blood glucose levels, promoting cellular uptake and lowering glucose. In contrast, glucagon acts to elevate blood glucose levels by promoting glycogen breakdown. Together, these two hormones work antagonistically to maintain blood glucose within precise physiological bounds. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
The adrenal cortex synthesises steroid hormones including glucocorticoids (such as cortisol). Glucocorticoids control carbohydrate, protein, and lipid metabolism, dampen inflammatory responses, and allow the body to adapt to physical and emotional stress. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q07 - Structural effects of denaturation on protein conformation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: During protein denaturation, the primary, secondary, and tertiary structures are destroyed as covalent peptide bonds are hydrolysed.

Statement II: The coagulation of egg white upon boiling and the curdling of milk by lactic acid bacteria are classic biological manifestations of protein denaturation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protein denaturation is the process where native proteins lose their higher-order three-dimensional structure due to changes in environmental factors such as temperature, pH, or salt concentration without the cleavage of peptide bonds.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
When a protein undergoes denaturation, only the secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures are disrupted because the stabilizing hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and electrostatic attractions are broken. The primary structure—defined by covalent peptide bonds linking the sequence of amino acids—remains completely intact during denaturation. Thus, Statement I is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Upon heating an egg, soluble albumin denatures, unfolds, and aggregates into an insoluble fibrous mass (coagulation of egg white). Similarly, in the curdling of milk, lactic acid produced by bacteria lowers the pH, causing the globular casein proteins to denature and precipitate. Both are classic examples of denaturation. Thus, Statement II is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_BIOMOLECULES_STATEMENT_Q08 - Amphoteric zwitterions and optical activity of amino acids

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In aqueous solution, \(\alpha\)-amino acids exhibit amphoteric behaviour because the zwitterionic \(-\mathrm{COO}^-\) group can accept a proton and the \(-\mathrm{NH}_3^+\) group can donate a proton.

Statement II: All naturally occurring \(\alpha\)-amino acids isolated from protein hydrolysis are optically active because their \(\alpha\)-carbon atoms are asymmetric.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Amino acids possess both carboxyl and amino functional groups. Internal acid-base neutralization creates dipolar zwitterions. Optical activity depends on the presence of an asymmetric (chiral) carbon bonded to four chemically distinct groups.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statement I
In water, amino acids exist primarily as dipolar zwitterions (\(\mathrm{R-CH(NH_3^+)-COO^-}\)). In the presence of a strong acid, the carboxylate anion (\(-\mathrm{COO}^-\)) acts as a base and accepts a proton. In the presence of a strong base, the ammonium cation (\(-\mathrm{NH}_3^+\)) acts as an acid and donates a proton. This allows amino acids to react with both acids and bases, demonstrating amphoteric character. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Statement II
Although 19 out of the 20 standard proteinogenic \(\alpha\)-amino acids possess a chiral \(\alpha\)-carbon and are optically active, glycine (\(\mathrm{H_2N-CH_2-COOH}\)) has two identical hydrogen atoms bonded to the \(\alpha\)-carbon. Because its \(\alpha\)-carbon is achiral, glycine is optically inactive. Therefore, not all naturally occurring \(\alpha\)-amino acids are optically active. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
